berridge.label: Wanting
berridge.note: Human fMRI food-cue reactivity is reduced in reward regions, though inconsistently and mostly in small studies; rodent progressive-ratio and cue-induced reinstatement data point the same way.

berridge.label: Liking
berridge.note: No rodent demonstration of a degraded orofacial liking response; the μ-opioid and CB1 hedonic hotspots are largely unprobed.

berridge.label: Learning
berridge.note: Barely studied. Reward-prediction-error and learning-rate effects are plausible given striatal and hippocampal changes, but uncharacterised.

berridge.label: Effort
berridge.note: Effort-discounting paradigms applied to GLP-1RAs are essentially absent — the cleanest assay of motivational anhedonia is missing.

tension.label: ⇄ tension
tension.note: Reconciliation candidates, none yet decisive: (a) temporal redistribution and recovery — anticipatory dopamine falls while consummatory dopamine is preserved or rises, and the suppression itself wanes with repeated dosing; (b) cumulative consumption falls through brainstem aversive channels rather than mesolimbic flattening; (c) animals pull harder for the remaining reward as food runs low. Zhu et al. (2025, Science) give candidate (a) direct support: photometry-calibrated optogenetics shows semaglutide suppresses VTA dopamine responsiveness during consumption, but the suppression — and palatable intake — recover over repeated dosing. A parallel preprint reports enhanced incentive value of small food rewards under chronic semaglutide — opposite to the canonical account. The reconciliation is an open question on the page, not a hedge in the prose.

fits.label: Wanting ↓ · cue-salience reduction
fits.note: Cross-reward mesolimbic gain reduction; strong randomised-trial support.

fits.label: Aversive interoception
fits.note: Central amygdala GABA arm; mild visceral malaise generalising to the drink.

fits.label: Liking change
fits.note: Possible but uncharacterised — no rodent liking assay has been run.

fits.label: Mood / anhedonia
fits.note: Possible in a subgroup; the population-level signal is neutral-to-favourable.

openQuestions: Does chronic exposure cause persistent recalibration of mesolimbic gain or reward-prediction-error signalling?
Effort-discounting under GLP-1RA is largely unstudied; sucrose preference conflates appetite with hedonics.
Does reduced wanting spread to non-consummatory motivation — social, sexual, achievement-related?
